sanskrit: mukhataḥ pātayām āsa śastreṇa niśitena ha nirviceṣṭaṃ bhujaṃgaṃ taṃ viśasya mṛgajīvanaḥ
english: The hunter, having cut it apart, struck the serpent's head with his sharp blade, knocking the motionless snake to the ground.

sanskrit: mokṣayitvā ca tāṃ vyādhaḥ prakṣālya salilena ca samāśvāsya kṛtāhārām atha papraccha bhārata
english: The hunter freed her, washed her with water, and having comforted her and given her food, he then questioned her, O Bharata.

sanskrit: kasya tvaṃ mṛgaśāvākṣi kathaṃ cābhyāgatā vanam kathaṃ cedaṃ mahat kṛcchraṃ prāptavaty asi bhāmini
english: "Whose are you, O doe-eyed one? How did you come to this forest? And how have you arrived at this great calamity, O lovely lady?"

sanskrit: damayantī tathā tena pṛcchyamānā viśāṃ pate sarvam etad yathāvṛttam ācacakṣe 'sya bhārata
english: Damayantī, thus questioned by him, O lord of peoples, narrated to him everything exactly as it had occurred, O Bharata.

sanskrit: tām ardhavastrasaṃvītāṃ pīnaśroṇipayodharām sukumārānavadyāṅgīṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām
english: Her — clad in only half a garment, with full hips and breasts, tender-limbed and blameless of form, her face like the full moon —

sanskrit: arālapakṣmanayanāṃ tathā madhurabhāṣiṇīm lakṣayitvā mṛgavyādhaḥ kāmasya vaśam eyivān
english: — with curving-lashed eyes, and sweet of speech — the deer-hunter, beholding her, fell under the sway of desire.

sanskrit: tām atha ślakṣṇayā vācā lubdhako mṛdupurvayā sāntvayām āsa kāmārtas tad abudhyata bhāminī
english: Then the hunter, tormented by desire, began to soothe her with smooth and gentle words; but the proud lady perceived it.

sanskrit: damayantī tu taṃ duṣṭam upalabhya pativratā tīvraroṣasamāviṣṭā prajajvāleva manyunā
english: But Damayantī, a devoted wife, perceiving that wicked man, was seized with fierce anger and blazed up as it were with fury.

sanskrit: sa tu pāpamatiḥ kṣudraḥ pradharṣayitum āturaḥ durdharṣāṃ tarkayām āsa dīptām agniśikhām iva
english: That vile man of evil mind, eager to violate her, reckoned her as one to be overpowered — like a blazing tongue of flame.

sanskrit: damayantī tu duḥkhārtā patirājyavinākṛtā atītavākpathe kāle śaśāpainaṃ ruṣā kila
english: But Damayantī, afflicted with grief, bereft of husband and kingdom, at the right moment — when speech was beyond him — cursed him in her wrath.

sanskrit: yathāhaṃ naiṣadhād anyaṃ manasāpi na cintaye tathāyaṃ patatāṃ kṣudraḥ parāsur mṛgajīvanaḥ
english: "As I have never thought of any man other than Naiṣadha, even in my mind, so let this vile hunter fall dead!"

sanskrit: uktamātre tu vacane tayā sa mṛgajīvanaḥ vyasuḥ papāta medinyām agnidagdha iva drumaḥ
english: The very moment the words were spoken by her, that hunter fell to the earth lifeless, like a tree struck by lightning.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca sā nihatya mṛgavyādhaṃ pratasthe kamalekṣaṇā vanaṃ pratibhayaṃ śūnyaṃ jhillikāgaṇanāditam
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Having slain the deer-hunter, she of lotus eyes set out into the forest — terrible, desolate, and resounding with swarms of crickets.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghravarāharkṣarurudvīpiniṣevitam nānāpakṣigaṇākīrṇaṃ mlecchataskarasevitam
english: It was haunted by lions, tigers, boars, bears, deer, and leopards, thronged with flocks of various birds, and frequented by barbarians and bandits.

sanskrit: śālaveṇudhavāśvatthatindukeṅgudakiṃśukaiḥ arjunāriṣṭasaṃchannaṃ candanaiś ca saśālmalaiḥ
english: It was covered with śāla, bamboo, dhava, aśvattha, tinduka, iṅguda, and kiṃśuka trees, with arjuna and ariṣṭa, with sandalwood and śālmalī.

sanskrit: jambvāmralodhrakhadiraśākavetrasamākulam kāśmaryāmalakaplakṣakadambodumbarāvṛtam
english: It was crowded with jambu, mango, lodhra, khadira, śāka, and vetasa, and encircled with kāśmarī, āmalaka, plakṣa, kadamba, and udumbara trees.

sanskrit: badarībilvasaṃchannaṃ nyagrodhaiś ca samākulam priyālatālakharjūraharītakabibhītakaiḥ
english: It was covered with badarī and bilva, thick with nyagrodha trees, and filled with priyāla, tāla, kharjūra, harītakī, and bibhītaka.

sanskrit: nānādhātuśatair naddhān vividhān api cācalān nikuñjān pakṣisaṃghuṣṭān darīś cādbhutadarśanāḥ nadīḥ sarāṃsi vāpīś ca vividhāṃś ca mṛgadvijān
english: She saw mountains bound with hundreds of various ores, diverse groves resounding with birds, caves of wondrous appearance, rivers, lakes, wells, and various animals and birds.

sanskrit: sā bahūn bhīmarūpāṃś ca piśācoragarākṣasān palvalāni taḍāgāni girikūṭāni sarvaśaḥ saritaḥ sāgarāṃś caiva dadarśādbhutadarśanān
english: She beheld many fearsome piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas, marshes and ponds, mountain peaks in every direction, and rivers and seas — all wonderful to behold.

sanskrit: yūthaśo dadṛśe cātra vidarbhādhipanandinī mahiṣān varāhān gomāyūn ṛkṣavānarapannagān
english: And there the daughter of Vidarbha's king beheld, in herds, buffaloes, boars, jackals, bears, monkeys, and serpents.

sanskrit: tejasā yaśasā sthityā śriyā ca parayā yutā vaidarbhī vicaraty ekā nalam anveṣatī tadā
english: Endowed with splendor, renown, steadfastness, and supreme beauty, the princess of Vidarbha wandered alone, then, searching for Nala.

sanskrit: nābibhyat sā nṛpasutā bhaimī tatrātha kasya cit dāruṇām aṭavīṃ prāpya bhartṛvyasanakarśitā
english: That princess, daughter of Bhīma, entering that dreadful forest, was not afraid of anything there, though worn by her husband's misfortune.

sanskrit: vidarbhatanayā rājan vilalāpa suduḥkhitā bhartṛśokaparītāṅgī śilātalasamāśritā
english: The daughter of Vidarbha, O king, wailed in deep sorrow, her body consumed by grief for her husband, leaning against a flat rock.

sanskrit: damayanty uvāca siṃhoraska mahābāho niṣadhānāṃ janādhipa kva nu rājan gato 'sīha tyaktvā māṃ nirjane vane
english: Damayantī said: "O lion-chested, mighty-armed lord of the Niṣadha people — where have you gone, O king, leaving me in this deserted forest?"

sanskrit: aśvamedhādibhir vīra kratubhiḥ svāptadakṣiṇaiḥ katham iṣṭvā naravyāghra mayi mithyā pravartase
english: "O hero, O tiger among men, having performed horse-sacrifices and other rites with full sacrificial fees — how do you now act falsely toward me?"

sanskrit: yat tvayoktaṃ naravyāghra matsamakṣaṃ mahādyute kartum arhasi kalyāṇa tad ṛtaṃ pārthivarṣabha
english: "That which you spoke, O tiger among men, of great splendor, in my presence — you should make that true, O auspicious one, O bull among kings."

sanskrit: yathoktaṃ vihagair haṃsaiḥ samīpe tava bhūmipa matsakāśe ca tair uktaṃ tad avekṣitum arhasi
english: "What was spoken by the geese, those birds, in your presence, O lord of earth, and what they said in my presence — that you should bear in mind."

sanskrit: catvāra ekato vedāḥ sāṅgopāṅgāḥ savistarāḥ svadhītā mānavaśreṣṭha satyam ekaṃ kilaikataḥ
english: "The four Vedas in full, with all their supplements and appendices, well studied, O best of men, weigh equally on one side; but Truth alone weighs on the other."

sanskrit: tasmād arhasi śatrughna satyaṃ kartuṃ nareśvara uktavān asi yad vīra matsakāśe purā vacaḥ
english: "Therefore you should make truth your deed, O destroyer of foes, O lord of men — do what you, O hero, once declared in my presence."

sanskrit: hā vīra nanu nāmāham iṣṭā kila tavānagha asyām aṭavyāṃ ghorāyāṃ kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase
english: "Alas, O hero! Was I not truly dear to you, O sinless one? Why do you not speak to me in this dreadful forest?"

sanskrit: bhartsayaty eṣa māṃ raudro vyāttāsyo dāruṇākṛtiḥ araṇyarāṭ kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ kiṃ māṃ na trātum arhasi
english: "This fierce lord of the forest, with gaping jaws and terrible form, hunger-maddened, threatens me — why do you not protect me?"

sanskrit: na me tvad anyā subhage priyā ity abravīs tadā tām ṛtāṃ kuru kalyāṇa puroktāṃ bhāratīṃ nṛpa
english: "'There is no one dear to me other than you, O fortunate one' — so you said then. Make those words true, O auspicious king."

sanskrit: unmattāṃ vilapantīṃ māṃ bhāryām iṣṭāṃ narādhipa īpsitām īpsito nātha kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase
english: "O lord of men, O my desired lord, why do you not speak to me — your beloved wife, distraught and wailing?"

sanskrit: kṛśāṃ dīnāṃ vivarṇāṃ ca malināṃ vasudhādhipa vastrārdhaprāvṛtām ekāṃ vilapantīm anāthavat
english: "Emaciated, wretched, pale, and soiled, O lord of earth, clad in half a garment, alone, wailing like one without protector —"

sanskrit: yūthabhraṣṭām ivaikāṃ māṃ hariṇīṃ pṛthulocana na mānayasi mānārha rudatīm arikarśana
english: "— like a doe separated from her herd, O wide-eyed one — why do you not regard me weeping, O crusher of foes, though you are worthy of honor?"

sanskrit: mahārāja mahāraṇye mām ihaikākinīṃ satīm ābhāṣamāṇāṃ svāṃ patnīṃ kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase
english: "O great king, in this great forest, why do you not speak to your devoted wife who calls out to you, left here alone?"

sanskrit: kulaśīlopasaṃpannaṃ cārusarvāṅgaśobhanam nādya tvām anupaśyāmi girāv asmin narottama vane cāsmin mahāghore siṃhavyāghraniṣevite
english: "Endowed with noble lineage and character, beautiful in every limb — I do not see you today, O best of men, on this mountain or in this dreadful forest frequented by lions and tigers."

sanskrit: śayānam upaviṣṭaṃ vā sthitaṃ vā niṣadhādhipa prasthitaṃ vā naraśreṣṭha mama śokavivardhana
english: "Whether lying down, or sitting, or standing, O lord of Niṣadha, or departing, O best of men — you are the one who increases my grief."

sanskrit: kaṃ nu pṛcchāmi duḥkhārtā tvadarthe śokakarśitā kaccid dṛṣṭas tvayāraṇye saṃgatyeha nalo nṛpaḥ
english: "Whom shall I ask, afflicted with sorrow, wasted by grief for your sake — 'Have you seen king Nala anywhere in this forest?'"

sanskrit: ko nu me kathayed adya vane 'smin viṣṭhitaṃ nalam abhirūpaṃ mahātmānaṃ paravyūhavināśanam
english: "Who today will tell me of Nala — handsome, noble-souled, destroyer of enemy arrays — dwelling in this forest?"

sanskrit: yam anveṣasi rājānaṃ nalaṃ padmanibhekṣaṇam ayaṃ sa iti kasyādya śroṣyāmi madhurāṃ giram
english: "The king Nala whom you seek, he of lotus-like eyes — whose sweet voice shall I hear today saying, 'Here he is'?"

sanskrit: araṇyarāḍ ayaṃ śrīmāṃś caturdaṃṣṭro mahāhanuḥ śārdūlo 'bhimukhaḥ praiti pṛcchāmy enam aśaṅkitā
english: "This glorious lord of the forest, the tiger with four fangs and great jaws, comes toward me — I shall question him without fear."

sanskrit: bhavān mṛgāṇām adhipas tvam asmin kānane prabhuḥ vidarbharājatanayāṃ damayantīti viddhi mām
english: "You are the lord of beasts, the master of this forest — know me as Damayantī, the daughter of the king of Vidarbha."

sanskrit: niṣadhādhipater bhāryāṃ nalasyāmitraghātinaḥ patim anveṣatīm ekāṃ kṛpaṇāṃ śokakarśitām āśvāsaya mṛgendreha yadi dṛṣṭas tvayā nalaḥ
english: "The wife of Nala, lord of Niṣadha, slayer of enemies — alone, wretched, worn by grief, seeking her husband — comfort her, O king of beasts, if you have seen Nala."

sanskrit: atha vāraṇyanṛpate nalaṃ yadi na śaṃsasi mām adasya mṛgaśreṣṭha viśokāṃ kuru duḥkhitām
english: "Or else, O lord of the forest, if you do not tell me of Nala, then devour me, O best of beasts, and free this grieving one from sorrow."

sanskrit: śrutvāraṇye vilapitaṃ mamaiṣa mṛgarāṭ svayam yāty etāṃ mṛṣṭasalilām āpagāṃ sāgaraṃgamām
english: Having heard my lament in the forest, the king of beasts himself goes away toward that clear-watered river flowing to the sea.

sanskrit: imaṃ śiloccayaṃ puṇyaṃ śṛṅgair bahubhir ucchritaiḥ virājadbhir divaspṛgbhir naikavarṇair manoramaiḥ
english: "This holy mountain with its many peaks, lofty, gleaming, sky-touching, of varied colors and lovely —"

sanskrit: nānādhātusamākīrṇaṃ vividhopalabhūṣitam asyāraṇyasya mahataḥ ketubhūtam ivocchritam
english: "— filled with various ores, adorned with diverse gems, rising like a banner of this great forest —"

sanskrit: siṃhaśārdūlamātaṅgavarāharkṣamṛgāyutam patatribhir bahuvidhaiḥ samantād anunāditam
english: "— filled with lions, tigers, elephants, boars, bears, and deer, resounding on all sides with many kinds of birds —"

sanskrit: kiṃśukāśokabakulapuṃnāgair upaśobhitam saridbhiḥ savihaṃgābhiḥ śikharaiś copaśobhitam girirājam imaṃ tāvat pṛcchāmi nṛpatiṃ prati
english: "— adorned with kiṃśuka, aśoka, bakula, and puṃnāga trees, beautified with bird-filled rivers and peaks — this king of mountains I shall now question concerning the king."

sanskrit: bhagavann acalaśreṣṭha divyadarśana viśruta śaraṇya bahukalyāṇa namas te 'stu mahīdhara
english: "O blessed best of mountains, of divine appearance, famous, a refuge, full of blessings — homage to you, O upholder of the earth!"

sanskrit: praṇame tvābhigamyāhaṃ rājaputrīṃ nibodha mām rājñaḥ snuṣāṃ rājabhāryāṃ damayantīti viśrutām
english: "I bow to you in approach — know me as a princess, daughter-in-law of a king, wife of a king, known by the name Damayantī."

sanskrit: rājā vidarbhādhipatiḥ pitā mama mahārathaḥ bhīmo nāma kṣitipatiḥ cāturvarṇyasya rakṣitā
english: "My father is the king, lord of Vidarbha, a great warrior — the lord of the earth named Bhīma, protector of the four social orders."

sanskrit: rājasūyāśvamedhānāṃ kratūnāṃ dakṣiṇāvatām āhartā pārthivaśreṣṭhaḥ pṛthucārvañcitekṣaṇaḥ
english: "The best of kings, he has performed rājasūya and aśvamedha sacrifices with full fees; broad and lovely are his slightly upturned eyes."

sanskrit: brahmaṇyaḥ sādhuvṛttaś ca satyavāg anasūyakaḥ śīlavān susamācāraḥ pṛthuśrīr dharmavic chuciḥ
english: "He is devoted to Brāhmaṇas, of virtuous conduct, truthful, free from envy, of good character, well-behaved, of broad glory, learned in dharma, and pure."

sanskrit: samyag goptā vidarbhāṇāṃ nirjitārigaṇaḥ prabhuḥ tasya māṃ viddhi tanayāṃ bhagavaṃs tvām upasthitām
english: "He is the proper guardian of the Vidarbhas, the lord who has conquered all enemies — know me, O blessed one, as his daughter who has come to you."

sanskrit: niṣadheṣu mahāśaila śvaśuro me nṛpottamaḥ sugṛhītanāmā vikhyāto vīrasena iti sma ha
english: "Among the Niṣadhas, O great mountain, my father-in-law is the best of kings, of auspicious name — famous as Vīrasena."

sanskrit: tasya rājñaḥ suto vīraḥ śrīmān satyaparākramaḥ kramaprāptaṃ pituḥ svaṃ yo rājyaṃ samanuśāsti ha
english: "His son is a hero, glorious, of true valor, who duly governs the kingdom that properly passed to him from his father."

sanskrit: nalo nāmāridamanaḥ puṇyaśloka iti śrutaḥ brahmaṇyo vedavid vāgmī puṇyakṛt somapo 'gnicit
english: "He is called Nala, subduer of foes, renowned as Puṇyaśloka — devoted to Brāhmaṇas, learned in the Vedas, eloquent, doer of righteous deeds, drinker of soma, builder of sacred fires."

sanskrit: yaṣṭā dātā ca yoddhā ca samyak caiva praśāsitā tasya mām acalaśreṣṭha viddhi bhāryām ihāgatām
english: "He is a sacrificer, a giver, a warrior, and a righteous ruler — know me, O best of mountains, as his wife who has come here."

sanskrit: tyaktaśriyaṃ bhartṛhīnām anāthāṃ vyasanānvitām anveṣamāṇāṃ bhartāraṃ taṃ vai naravarottamam
english: "I am bereft of fortune, husbandless, without protector, beset by misfortune, searching for that best of men, my husband."

sanskrit: kham ullikhadbhir etair hi tvayā śṛṅgaśatair nṛpaḥ kaccid dṛṣṭo 'calaśreṣṭha vane 'smin dāruṇe nalaḥ
english: "With these hundreds of peaks that scrape the sky — have you seen the king, O best of mountains, in this dreadful forest? Has Nala been seen by you?"

sanskrit: gajendravikramo dhīmān dīrghabāhur amarṣaṇaḥ vikrāntaḥ satyavāg dhīro bhartā mama mahāyaśāḥ niṣadhānām adhipatiḥ kaccid dṛṣṭas tvayā nalaḥ
english: "My husband — of the prowess of a lordly elephant, wise, long-armed, intolerant of insult, valiant, truthful, steadfast, of great renown, lord of the Niṣadhas — has he, Nala, been seen by you?"

sanskrit: kiṃ māṃ vilapatīm ekāṃ parvataśreṣṭha duḥkhitām girā nāśvāsayasy adya svāṃ sutām iva duḥkhitām
english: "Why do you not comfort me with your voice today, O best of mountains, wailing alone in sorrow, as a father would his grieving daughter?"

sanskrit: vīra vikrānta dharmajña satyasaṃdha mahīpate yady asy asmin vane rājan darśayātmānam ātmanā
english: "O hero, O valiant one, O knower of dharma, O king of steadfast truth — if you are in this forest, O king, reveal yourself by yourself."

sanskrit: kadā nu snigdhagambhīrāṃ jīmūtasvanasaṃnibhām śroṣyāmi naiṣadhasyāhaṃ vācaṃ tām amṛtopamām
english: "When shall I hear that affectionate, deep voice of the Niṣadha king, resembling the sound of a cloud — that speech of his, like nectar?"

sanskrit: vaidarbhīty eva kathitāṃ śubhāṃ rājño mahātmanaḥ āmnāyasāriṇīm ṛddhām mama śokanibarhiṇīm
english: "That auspicious speech of the noble king, simply saying 'O Vaidarbhī,' flowing like a sacred text, rich, the destroyer of my grief?"

sanskrit: iti sā taṃ giriśreṣṭham uktvā pārthivanandinī damayantī tato bhūyo jagāma diśam uttarām
english: Having spoken thus to that best of mountains, the princess Damayantī, daughter of a king, then set off again toward the northern direction.

sanskrit: sā gatvā trīn ahorātrān dadarśa paramāṅganā tāpasāraṇyam atulaṃ divyakānanadarśanam
english: After traveling for three days and nights, that most excellent of women beheld an incomparable hermit-forest, of divine woodland appearance.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhabhṛgvatrisamais tāpasair upaśobhitam niyataiḥ saṃyatāhārair damaśaucasamanvitaiḥ
english: It was adorned by ascetics equal to Vasiṣṭha, Bhṛgu, and Atri — disciplined, controlled in diet, possessed of self-restraint and purity.

sanskrit: abbhakṣair vāyubhakṣaiś ca patrāhārais tathaiva ca jitendriyair mahābhāgaiḥ svargamārgadidṛkṣubhiḥ
english: Among them were those who subsisted on water, those who lived on air, and those who ate only leaves — masters of their senses, greatly blessed, desirous of seeing the path to heaven.

sanskrit: valkalājinasaṃvītair munibhiḥ saṃyatendriyaiḥ tāpasādhyuṣitaṃ ramyaṃ dadarśāśramamaṇḍalam
english: She beheld a lovely hermitage-grove, inhabited by ascetics, sages clad in bark garments and hides, with restrained senses.

sanskrit: sā dṛṣṭvaivāśramapadaṃ nānāmṛganiṣevitam śākhāmṛgagaṇaiś caiva tāpasaiś ca samanvitam
english: Seeing the hermitage frequented by various animals, thronged with troops of monkeys, and accompanied by ascetics —

sanskrit: subhrūḥ sukeśī suśroṇī sukucā sudvijānanā varcasvinī supratiṣṭhā svañcitodyatagāminī
english: — she of beautiful brows, lovely hair, shapely hips, fine breasts, and beautiful teeth-adorned face, radiant, of noble bearing, moving with a graceful, lofty gait —

sanskrit: sā viveśāśramapadaṃ vīrasenasutapriyā yoṣidratnaṃ mahābhāgā damayantī manasvinī
english: — she, the beloved wife of Vīrasena's son, a gem of womanhood, greatly blessed, the spirited Damayantī, entered that hermitage.

sanskrit: sābhivādya tapovṛddhān vinayāvanatā sthitā svāgataṃ ta iti proktā taiḥ sarvais tāpasaiś ca sā
english: She greeted the elders in austerity and stood with bowed reverence; all the ascetics there welcomed her, saying, "Welcome."

sanskrit: pūjāṃ cāsyā yathānyāyaṃ kṛtvā tatra tapodhanāḥ āsyatām ity athocus te brūhi kiṃ karavāmahe
english: The wealth-in-austerity ascetics honored her duly, then said, "Be seated" and "Tell us — what may we do for you?"

sanskrit: tān uvāca varārohā kaccid bhagavatām iha tapasy agniṣu dharmeṣu mṛgapakṣiṣu cānaghāḥ kuśalaṃ vo mahābhāgāḥ svadharmacaraṇeṣu ca
english: The lovely-hipped one asked them: "O sinless ones, O greatly blessed ones, is all well with you here — in your austerities, sacred fires, in dharma, among the animals and birds, and in the practice of your own dharma?"

sanskrit: tair uktā kuśalaṃ bhadre sarvatreti yaśasvinī brūhi sarvānavadyāṅgi kā tvaṃ kiṃ ca cikīrṣasi
english: Told by them that all was well, O fortunate one, the renowned and perfectly-limbed one was addressed: "Tell us — who are you, and what do you wish to do?"

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva te paraṃ rūpaṃ dyutiṃ ca paramām iha vismayo naḥ samutpannaḥ samāśvasihi mā śucaḥ
english: "On seeing your supreme beauty and supreme radiance here, wonder has arisen in us — take courage, do not grieve."
